rationale: The workflow runs a large Ruby matrix (sqlite, mysql, postgres jobs across many Ruby versions and gemfiles) and already uses ruby/setup-ruby@v1 with bundler-cache: true. The measured experiment batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-3d6f1c5a422aa116-r2 (pattern P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE) shows that adding an explicit actions/cache@v4 step for vendor/bundle on top of bundler-cache: true reduced median elapsed time by 10.53% (171s to 153s) with all 3/3 runs successful in both arms, preserving test coverage. The same dependency-caching principle applies to all three jobs in this workflow. The cache key includes runner OS, Ruby version, gemfile name, and a hash of the gemfile, with hierarchical restore keys for broader hits. No permissions are weakened, no secrets or network access are added, and all build/test steps are preserved unchanged.
